name: CIS Controls
source: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1, OSCAL catalog published by the Center for Internet Security: https://bitbucket.org/cis-it-workspace/cis-controls-v8.1_oscal/src/main/src/catalogs/json/cis-controls-v8.1_catalog.json (catalog metadata version 8.1.2, last-modified 2025-04-09)
notes: Official CIS-published OSCAL serialization of the CIS Controls v8.1 (18 control groups, 153 safeguards). The OSCAL catalog's own metadata version is 8.1.2, i.e. a revision of the v8.1 document; safeguard content and ids are the v8.1 set. This is v8.1, not v8.0 (v8.0 has 146 safeguards and lacks e.g. 16.14 Threat Modeling), and it is the Controls framework, not the per-platform CIS Benchmarks. Titles are the OSCAL control titles, which are the official safeguard titles. OSCAL ids 'cisc-<group>.<safeguard>' were normalised to '<group>.<safeguard>'.
cross_check: All 18 control-group titles compared against CIS's own controls list; the 18 per-group safeguard counts sum to 153; every group's safeguards are contiguous; 1.1 and 18.5 hand-checked against the published titles.

group_reasons.1: an asset-inventory process: the inventory itself is not something a scan of the target observes
group_reasons.2: a software-inventory or allowlisting process, not a technical artefact a network scan produces
group_reasons.3: a data-governance process (classification, retention, disposal or loss prevention): the process leaves no artefact a scan can observe
group_reasons.4: a configuration safeguard on an endpoint or network device ARACHNE does not administer; it needs host-level access this scanner deliberately does not have
group_reasons.5: an account-lifecycle process (dormant-account review, service-account inventory): it needs directory-administrator or HR data
group_reasons.6: an access-governance process: granting and revoking access is an administrative act, not a network artefact
group_reasons.7: a patch-management or remediation process step: patching is performed by the estate rather than observed by a scan
group_reasons.8: a log-collection or log-retention activity in the operator's own estate
group_reasons.9: a browser, mail-client or DNS-filter configuration on managed endpoints
group_reasons.10: an endpoint anti-malware deployment or signature-management safeguard
group_reasons.11: a backup, recovery or recovery-testing process
group_reasons.12: a network-infrastructure management process for devices ARACHNE does not administer
group_reasons.13: a security-monitoring or traffic-filtering capability deployed in the estate
group_reasons.14: a security-awareness training activity for the workforce
group_reasons.15: a service-provider governance process (contracts, classification, decommissioning)
group_reasons.16: an application-security process step (threat modelling, developer training, root-cause analysis) with no artefact a scan produces
group_reasons.18: a penetration-test programme activity performed by the estate

default_reason: no shipped ARACHNE check produces evidence about this control
